newsitem.title: JORDAN: AMMAN STOCKS BUOYED BY IRAQ TRADE PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: AMMAN STOCKS BUOYED BY IRAQ TRADE PROSPECTS.

text.p: Jordan's official index fell on Tuesday but the overall market was buoyed by investor optimism over better prospects of trade with Iraq under the second phase of the U.N.'s "oil-for-food" deal, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.36 percent to 165.78 points in 917,673 dinar ($1.3 million) turnover.

"It's an upward trend based on forecast of better corporate earnings and improved trade with Iraq and steps towards more lifting of U.N. sanctions against Baghdad," said Nasser al-Amad of United Financial Investments.
The busiest traded stocks were mostly of firms expected to benefit from additional export orders under the second phase of Iraq's oil-for-food deal.
Jordan Selpho Chemicals rose five percent to 0.63 dinars while Intermediate Petrochemicals rose to 0.57 dinars from 0.55.

Investor hopes were raised after positive remarks by visiting Iraqi ministers to Jordan over the last few days who said they expected Jordanian industry to do well from Baghdad's U.N. deal, citing confidence in the competitiveness of its exports.
Jordanian industry, which won $120 million of orders for humanitarian goods under the first six-month stage of the oil-for-food accord, hopes to do even better under the new deal.
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, lost 1.25 dinars to 293 in trade of just 340 shares.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcements of a bonus share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
But cancellation of the 50 percent foreign ownership ceiling has been delayed in cabinet, deflating the Arab Bank bubble.
Overall 21 shares rose on Tuesday and 10 fell, with another 16 trading but closing unchanged. $1 = 0.709 dinars
